title: Silent Suffering: Using Machine Learning to Measure CEO Depression

scopes.description: Complete supplied workflow: DAIC-WOZ model preparation, CapitalIQ audio/transcript processing, the native SAS Enterprise Guide project and its embedded SAS stages/macros, EGP exports to Python 11/12 and the returned imports in the original interleaved order, quarterly and annual panel construction, and Stata analyses. The EGP ZIP remains a statically inspected workflow container rather than a registered text entry point. The separate annual guidance branch is retained and lacks a supplied annual Python producer; execution is unverified.

issues.description: The bounded EGP inspection identifies separate raw-library inputs: quarterly and annual premerged Compustat–CRSP tables; CRSP daily, monthly, name-history and Compustat-link products; I/B/E/S EPS and revenue summaries, a separate I/B/E/S–CRSP link, and guidance; plus execucomp, ISS directors, firm_age/firm_age_ann, instown and short_interest. Existing individual probes verify readable local CRSP DSF/MSF/MSENAMES/CCMXPF, Execucomp ANNCOMP and EPS-summary products with their actual underlying fields. The prepared quarterly/annual merges, firm-age producers, revenue-measure and linkage contracts, guidance assembly, ISS mapping, instown mapping and short-interest measure remain specific unresolved contracts. COMP.FUNDQ/FUNDA and other component probes do not prove a supplied producer for either premerged table. EGP exports to Python and the final master panels are generated intermediates, not independent preloaded roots; no full-history or original-byte gate is imposed on compatible local sources.

Python 08.01 reads feature_gemaps.csv in its training branches, but no supplied program produces that feature table. The specific feature extraction recipe, required fields and split construction remain unknown; DAIC audio/labels alone do not establish this prepared input.
Dependency D0001 daicwoz_index_combined.csv is consumed by the CNN branch and has no supplied producer. The exact index fields and its participant-to-image mapping are not verified.

Python 08.02 expects train and validation spectrogram image directories. No active image-writing statement or matching packaged directory was found in the supplied source/inventory; the comment in Python 09 about spectrograms is not an active image producer.

Dependency D0002 df_concat_index2.csv is read by Python 08.03 but has no supplied producer. Its source_dir/split/category/embedding-name and PHQ8 mapping, and its relation to the stage-02 embedding output, remain unresolved.

Dependency D0003 ciq_w_audio_links_w_ceo_names_from_execucomp_and_ciq.csv is read by Python 10 but has no supplied producer among the registered Python sources or active EGP exports. The call-to-CEO matching fields, rules, population and crosswalk to imported EGP tables remain unresolved.

The supplied Python 05 entrypoint selects index_file_test.csv under a diarization_test directory and uses a test-oriented default. This does not establish a full-sample linkage input or the production call/audio/transcript coverage; the full-run parameter and input mapping need to be set in a working copy.

Python 09 unpickles a scaler and YAMNet-SVR model from author-local paths. The package contains neither artifact, and supplied training scripts do not produce or serialize the named deployment files. Feature order, preprocessing, model/scaler definitions and compatible dimensions remain unknown; no executable object was loaded.

Python 04 names the pyAudioAnalysis svm_rbf_sm classifier resource, but the required file/revision and a compatible acquisition or local route are not established. The dependency package is not available in the metadata probe.

The EGP exports guidance_cessation_ann_input_for_python.csv and later imports an annual eps_guide_cessation file, but the package supplies only the quarterly Python 11 producer. No annual Python producer or equivalent active EGP transformation for eps_guide_cessation is supplied, so this annual branch cannot be closed by the quarterly output.

evidence.description: README overview: Python stage order and SAS-to-Stata handoff, with small-subsample logs.
evidence.quote:
This document provides an overview of the codes used to generate our final sample. Running
the Python code files sequentially produces the final datasets. For the purpose of generating log files
required by the journal, a small subsample of the primary dataset is used. This approach is necessary
because running the code for the full dataset is computationally intensive. The supercomputers at
Indiana University and the University of Kentucky were utilized to process the entire data set, the
code being submitted as batch jobs that do not generate log files.
   The final data sets produced by the Python scripts are subsequently merged in the SAS project
file, which serves as the input for the regression analyses conducted in the Stata file. Below is a brief
description of each code file:

For training the depression score estimation model, we used the DAIC-WOZ dataset collected
  by the USC Institute for Creative Technologies. The dataset is available to academics and
  other non-profit researchers upon signing an agreement form. We used commercially licensed

evidence.description: Datasheet summarizes the intended training, audio, data-construction, merge, and regression sequence.
evidence.quote:
• Download DAIC-WOZ dataset.
     • Train machine learning model to estimate depression score.
     • Download audio files and transcripts of conference calls from CapitalIQ Browser Plat-
       form.
     • Diarization of audio files to extract the part that CEO speaks during the presentation
       part.
     • Process the CEO part audio files and deploy the trained model to estimate CEO Depres-
       sion Score.
     • Collect data from sources mentioned above and detailed in the main text of the paper to
       create the variables needed for the analyses.
     • Merge datasets together.
     • Run the regression models.

review_notes: Static assessment covers every registered Python, Stata and EGP code container and the frozen seven dependency IDs. EGP ZIP/XML inspection was bounded and hash-bound; raw project XML and full author path literals remain withheld. The project contains 18 SAS code blocks and active import/export stages; no EG/SAS author program, model, regression, parser trial, or data generation was run.

The annual EGP guidance import has no supplied annual Python producer. Python 09's prediction output is timestamped and must be aligned with the EGP import configuration in a portable copy.
